title: World Shaper — Upgrade Options
summary: Hearthhull, the Worldseed drains each opponent for 2 whenever you sacrifice a land, and once stationed it trades lands for cards. The stock list ramps far more than it needs to, is top-heavy, and has no way to protect its key pieces. Budget: up to €20 per deck in total (Cardmarket prices).

notes: Hearthhull's drain ('whenever you sacrifice a land, each opponent loses 2 life') is part of its 8+ station box, so it only works once Hearthhull has 8 charge counters. You station it by tapping creatures, adding counters equal to their power, so the deck needs creatures with high power (Juri, Uurg, Centaur Vinecrasher, Ob Nixilis, Moraug).
Top-heavy: 15 nonland cards cost 5 or more (World Breaker 7, Omnath 7, three 6-drops, nine 5-drops).
Too much ramp: 42 lands plus ~15 ramp pieces. Some ramp spells can become engines.
No protection at all for the commander or the board.
Interaction is good: ~10 spot removal, 6 at instant speed, 4 board wipes.
Mana base: Wastes is a colourless basic in a three-colour deck and should go.

Commander check: the card search flags that Hearthhull has no 'can be your commander' text (it's an artifact, not a creature). It is the precon's face commander, so check with your playgroup. Szarel, Genesis Shepherd (already in the deck) can legally be your commander.

core.name: Core package
core.description: Cheap protection (Tamiyo's Safekeeping covers Hearthhull before it's a creature; Snakeskin Veil covers creatures), plus a free outlet that turns any land into a 2-life drain with Hearthhull. It also removes the colourless Wastes. Planetary Annihilation stays: with Hearthhull at 8+, Mayhem Devil and Juri, a mass land sacrifice is a finisher.

swaps.why: One mana: hexproof and indestructible on any permanent, including Hearthhull before it becomes a creature. Satyr Wayfinder is a weak 2-drop that only digs for a land.
One mana: hexproof and a +1/+1 counter on a creature, which counters a removal spell. Escape to the Wilds is a 5-mana card-draw spell; Tannuk and Hearthhull cover card draw.
0 mana: sacrifice a land and gain 2 life. With Hearthhull, each opponent also loses 2, so any spare land becomes a drain, at instant speed. Wastes produces colourless mana in a three-colour deck.

directions.name: Scorched Earth Drain
directions.pitch: Sacrifice lands every turn and replay them from the graveyard. Landfall pingers (Tannuk, Sabotender, Hagra, Ob Nixilis) deal damage from turn 2; once Hearthhull is stationed to 8, each sacrificed land also drains 2, and Planetary Annihilation becomes a finisher. Juri, Countryside Crusher and Ob Nixilis grow with every land played or sacrificed, so they station Hearthhull quickly.
directions.plays_like: Burns the table out with land sacrifices

swaps.why: Play lands from your graveyard, so every sacrificed land comes back. Skyshroud Claim is a fourth 4-mana ramp spell in a deck with too much ramp.
A second way to replay lands from your graveyard, and it can also recast a permanent from there. Cultivate is redundant ramp.
Every land that enters pings each opponent for 1, from turn 2 on, before Hearthhull is stationed. Night's Whisper is generic draw; Hearthhull's own 2+ ability draws two cards per land.

Every land that enters pings each opponent for 1, and the second trigger each turn draws a card. With Hearthhull's extra land play and lands replayed from the graveyard, that happens most turns. Groundskeeper's 'return a basic land' is redundant now that Ramunap, Conduit and Szarel let you play lands straight from the graveyard.
Each land that enters drains each opponent 1, or gives a creature deathtouch.

Gets a +1/+1 counter every time a land goes to your graveyard (every Zuran Orb, Hearthhull or fetch-land sacrifice), so it grows fast and stations Hearthhull. Each upkeep it mills lands off your library, which Ramunap, Conduit and Szarel let you play. Gaze of Granite also destroys your own cheap permanents (Zuran Orb, Juri, Geopede); Blasphemous Act and Pest Infestation remain as wipes.
Every land that enters drains a player for 3 and puts three +1/+1 counters on Ob Nixilis, which makes it the best creature for stationing Hearthhull. World Breaker costs 7.

Land swap. When it enters you sacrifice two lands: with Hearthhull at 8+ that's 4 drain to each opponent, plus Juri counters, Mayhem Devil pings and two lands for Ramunap to replay. Then it taps for three mana of one colour. Viridescent Bog can't make mana on its own ({1},{T} only).
Land swap. Sacrifices itself for a basic: one drain trigger, then a second landfall, which makes Tannuk draw. Bojuka Bog enters tapped for a one-time graveyard exile.

directions.name: Landfall Army
directions.pitch: Turn the deck's extra land drops into creature tokens, mana and damage. Hearthhull's extra land plays and the sacrifice-and-replay loop trigger landfall several times a turn.
directions.plays_like: Wide board of tokens; explosive turns

swaps.why: Every land that enters makes a Treasure or a Food. Ramp that keeps paying off, unlike a one-shot sorcery.
Play an extra land each turn, and return lands to your hand to replay them for more landfall.
Every land that enters pings each opponent for 1.
Every land that enters drains a player for 3 and grows Ob Nixilis.
A 1/1 Saproling on every landfall; with extra land drops and replays, that's several tokens a turn.
Makes a Plant per basic land when it enters, and every landfall puts four +1/+1 counters on a Plant.
A same-cost 7-drop that wins games: a 0/1 Plant per land you control, and every landfall grows them all. It also fuels Phylath.

directions.name: Lands Recursion
directions.pitch: Treat your graveyard as a second hand of lands. Loop Life from the Loam, replay lands with Crucible effects, and draw cards off discarded lands. This direction grinds out the longest games.
directions.plays_like: Grindy value; never runs out of cards

swaps.why: Return three lands from your graveyard to your hand, and dredge it back instead of drawing to keep the loop going. Endless fuel for Hearthhull.
Play lands from your graveyard, and recast a permanent from there each turn.
2 mana: your lands have hexproof, and for {2} you return a land from your graveyard to your hand. Moraug is a 6-drop.
Returns two lands from your graveyard to your hand when it enters, for more sacrifice fuel.
Makes a Plant whenever lands hit your graveyard (each Hearthhull activation), and can return a land by sacrificing three creatures.
Grows on landfall; discard a creature to put a land from your graveyard onto the battlefield.
Mills lands off the top every upkeep (Loam fuel) and grows whenever a land hits your graveyard. A 3-drop instead of a 7-drop.

recommendation: Scorched Earth Drain uses Hearthhull best: the landfall pingers deal damage from turn 2, and once Hearthhull is stationed to 8 every sacrifice and replay is another 2-point drain. All three directions stay under €20 including the core package.
